sections.heading: C2 — KG hints for Traffic Signals
sections.markdown:
## C2 — KG hints for Traffic Signals

FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A01
A right turn on red is allowed from any street after a stop unless signed otherwise, while a left turn on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto a one-way street [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint turns-on-red; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec08-F04 and sec08-F05.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A03
A flashing red signal requires a full stop like a stop sign, while a flashing yellow signal allows you to proceed with caution [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint flashing-signals; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec08-F11 and sec08-F12.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A04
A steady yellow X orders you out of the lane, while a flashing yellow X permits the lane only for preparing a left turn [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint lane-control; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec08-F15 and sec08-F16.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A02
A green light allows going straight or turning unless signs prohibit, while a green arrow allows movement only in the arrow's direction [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint arrows; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec08-F07 and sec08-F09.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A01
A yellow light warns that red is coming and you should avoid entering, while entering after the red light appears is flatly prohibited [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint three-color; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec08-F06 and sec08-F03.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A04
A flashing DON'T WALK lets pedestrians already crossing finish, while a steady DON'T WALK forbids entering the roadway toward the signal [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint pedestrian-signals; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec08-F18 and sec08-F19.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec08-R07 | anchor: A03
A red X lane control signal means the lane belongs to opposing traffic, while a red arrow means stop for that lane just as a red light would [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint lane-control; prereq_hint sec08-R03; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec08-F14 and sec08-F08.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec08-R08 | anchor: A01
With no stop line you stop before the crosswalk, while with neither stop line nor crosswalk you stop before entering the intersection [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint three-color; prereq_hint sec08-R05; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec08-F03 and sec08-F04.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec08-R09 | anchor: A02
A green light requires yielding to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection, while a right turn on red requires yielding to all pedestrians and all vehicles [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint yielding; prereq_hint sec08-R01; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec08-F07 and sec08-F04.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-R10 | anchor: A04
A flashing WALK warns of a possible pedestrian-vehicle conflict, while a steady WALK simply permits crossing toward the signal [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint pedestrian-signals; prereq_hint sec08-R06; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec08-F19 and sec08-F18.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0042]

corpus_stability.reason: The Hawaii Driver's Manual is a periodically reprinted reference (imprint HMG 5/2023, copyright line through 2023); the standard three-color signals, turns on red, lighted arrows, combination signals, flashing signals, lane control signals and pedestrian signals rules on pages 39–42 are statutory and procedural content that changes less than once a year, so no BlockedProbe.
